stories.title: Tech wreck drags Anthropic into the red on its second day of trading
stories.summary: Nasdaq futures trade lower after steep declines extend across global tech stocks

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Tech wreck drags Anthropic into the red on its second day of trading
sources.text: This is CNBC's Morning Squawk newsletter. Subscribe here to receive future editions in your inbox. Hello, this is Leonie Kidd with today's edition of Morning Squawk. Despite its debut-day rally, the broader markets plunged around the stock, and it's now catching the tech cold - down in premarket trading on its second day as a public company. It's day 2 and Anthropic shares are under pressure. The stock is falling in premarket trading , at one point down over 6%. The stock had closed 17% higher in its first day of trading, easing back from a near-40% jump earlier in the session. Speaking exclusively to CNBC's Andrew Ross Sorkin after ringing the bell at the Nasdaq, CEO Dario Amodei defended the company's massive $900 billion in AI commitments, saying, "If you look at the amount of cash we have on the balance sheet and the amount of revenue that we're already making per year, suddenly those commitments don't seem so large." Nasdaq futures are back in the red, underperforming both the Dow and S&P in early trading. Nvidia is lower in premarket trading, alongside AMD . It's a deeply negative handover from Asia and Europe. Japan's Softbank suffered its worst trading day in over two years as the AI sell-off swept through the Asian tech sector. Shares in CXMT , SK Hynix and others ended the day deep in the red. In Europe, chip stocks like ASML , Infineon and others suffered heavy selling. The debate over the export of U.S.-made chips to China has divided the Trump Administration's cabinet. The Nvidia scandal has further exposed this split and fanned the flames between the two camps. CNBC's Morning Squawk recaps the biggest stories investors should know before the stock market opens, every weekday morning. Bitcoin hit a 4-month low amid the broader tech sell-off, putting further pressure on cryptocurrencies . Precious metals investors can be forgiven if they feel like the past year has given them whiplash. Following a torrid run in which the price of gold hit new records 53 times in 2025, it hit a historic high of $5,589.38 an ounce on Jan. 28, only to take an almost equally historic nosedive. On Wednesday, gold fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025, roughly a third below its peak. A convergence of factors pushed gold to historic highs earlier this year, according to Suki Cooper, global head of commodities research at Standard Chartered, the London-based multinational bank. Now a different convergence is bringing the price down. — CNBC's Alexa LoMonaco, Shikhar Gupta, Vanna Ben'Ous, Daren Fonda, Chloe Taylor, Luke Fountain, and Kevin Williams contributed to this report.

sources.name: The Guardian Technology
sources.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading
sources.text: The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn? As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory. Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal. Shares in the frontier AI company behind the Claude chatbot, which floated in the US on Thursday, fell by 9% on Friday, ceding most of the gains from the biggest initial public offering in history. They dropped to $88.30, towards the $83 level at which Anthropic priced its stock market debut. Anthropic’s first two days as a listed company have been volatile. Its shares jumped by 17% on Thursday, after briefly surging by almost 40% when trading in the firm began. US technology stocks followed Anthropic down on Friday, with the memory chipmaker SanDisk falling 14% and rival Micron down 12%. Nvidia fell 14%, eliminating hundreds of billions of dollars in market cap. Neil Wilson, a UK investor strategist at Saxo, said there was “just relentless selling in tech”. He warned: “Anthropic shares tumbled to take an $85 handle as the post-IPO euphoria gives way to the reality of a steep sell-off across the tech and AI space that shows no sign of easing just yet.” Global markets slumped on Friday too; Asian stock markets recorded their worst week since 2020, as shares in big chip companies fell. In Taiwan, stocks dropped 6.7% to hit their lowest point since mid-April, with the chip maker TSMC down about 6%. The scale of the decline in Taiwan prompted the chair of its stock exchange to pledge to ensure the stable operation ⁠of capital markets, and reassure investors they should remain confident in the fundamentals of Taiwanese companies. In Japan, the Nikkei index fell 5%, while South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi index lost 5.5%. Shares in the tech investor SoftBank had their worst day in more than two years, down 14.5% in Tokyo, amid worries around its aggressive bets on AI. European stock markets posted their biggest weekly loss since March 2025, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 dropping 1.9% on Friday. London’s blue-chip stock index hit a five-month low. The sell-off followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, where the main indices all fell by more than 2% on a day dominated by Anthropic’s IPO . Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, said Anthropic could be “draining market liquidity”, as investors sell shares in other companies to raise funds to pay for stock in the newly floated AI firm. “The slide from yesterday’s highs sends a message that there might be more at work here than investors realise, and while brokers are scrambling to buy more, that liquidity has to come from somewhere, and the other tech names may be the first ones to feel the pressure,” Beauchamp said. Anthropic’s flotation has failed to ease worries around the AI trade, as investors increasingly question whether companies can deliver the returns necessary to justify the billions of dollars being poured into the AI buildout. Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at Capital.com, said: “The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending. “The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run. The weakness in equal-weighted indices suggests that selling pressure is no longer confined to a handful of technology giants, while Europe’s recent outperformance has also faded.” Nvidia shares fell byafter California served the chip company with a subpoena as part of an investigation into whether its advanced semiconductors ended up in China. Britain’s FTSE 100 share index dropped by 5.1% this week, its biggest weekly fall since the start of the Iran war. Fears that US central bankers may raise interest rates to fight inflation have lifted the dollar to a 19-month high, and pushed down the gold price – with gold on track for its worst week since March. Bitcoin hit its lowest level in four months, dropping below the $60,000 point for the first time since early July.

While some have already spent hours immersed in the...

sources.name: The Guardian Technology
sources.title: ‘The greatest game ever made’: readers and Guardian staff on Grand Theft Auto VI
sources.text: Rockstar’s newest installment of its hit franchise still has plenty of action, along with a dose of ‘healthy masculinity’ D escribed as the biggest entertainment launch in history, the new Grand Theft Auto game has prompted avid fans around the world to take the day off work, stock up on snacks and celebrate its arrival after 13 years of waiting. While some have already spent hours immersed in the game’s criminal escapades, others have found themselves doing household chores, building houses or simply taking in the scenery – which includes more than 170 flora and fauna species native to Florida . GTA VI has generated extraordinary global anticipation for its action-packed gameplay, but players are now finding new delight in the game’s more intimate moments. From the relationship between protagonists Jason and Lucia to the painstaking world-building of Leonida, Rockstar’s fictional take on Florida, players have shared their wide-ranging experiences with the Guardian, revealing what has surprised and challenged them about this long-awaited release – and what this all means for the series’ evolution. Pete Langhelt, 39, from Colchester, pre-ordered GTA VI “as soon as I could”, and has been looking forward to its release for a long time. “Out of my group of friends I’m probably the only one really nerding out about it,” he says. While Pete hasn’t been able to take time from work in the civil service, he’s still clocked “about 10 hours” of gameplay already. “The core of the missions themselves are pretty similar,” he says. “You turn up somewhere, shoot a load of people and escape. But the development of the characters has changed an awful lot. I have enjoyed the dynamic between Jason and Lucia. I never thought you could make comfortable domesticity into an enjoyable side activity in a video game.” Pete has played all the installments of GTA franchise from the first, when he was “probably too young to be playing”. “I think Red Dead Redemption 2 was my favourite Rockstar game going into this, and it seems to have developed the things that I really liked about Red Dead.” The game encourages exploration, he says. “The day and night cycle seems a lot less intense than GTA V, meaning you don’t feel rushed to get things done. I can let Jason take a slow start to the day before taking a slow drive or boat ride to whatever criminal activity needs completing.” His partner is less keen. “She’ll have to put up with me being on the Xbox for the next few weeks,” he says. A 59-year-old MBA retiree from Venice, Florida, was also struck by just how much of the experience revolves around everyday life. He described it as the “most beautiful, real, open-world game that’s ever existed”. “I was surprised that, with about 10-plus hours of play, most of my time has been spent performing mundane tasks like home repair, grocery shopping, personal grooming and trying to open a bank account. The realism is incredible, but perhaps too real,” he said. “It’s as fully realized as a game world could be. I never expected to see anything more fully developed,” he added. Rob Smeraldo, 28, from Dundee, took the day off work yesterday to play the game on his PlayStation 5. “I made sure I had loads of snacks and Domino’s,” he says. And already, Rob believes that “GTA VI must be the greatest game ever made”. “I think the realism and just the detail put into it is absolutely astounding. The shadows, the way the hair moves when people move around … They took their time, but it’s definitely been worth it,” he says. Rob is a longtime GTA fan and wore a GTA VI T-shirt and drank from a GTA mug to mark the occasion. “I purchased the physical copy [of the game] as soon as it became purchasable – I just wanted the memorabilia, you know?” Ella Delancey, 35, of Berkshire has been playing GTA since she was a child. “GTA III is a huge core memory for me. My brother and I were much too young to be playing it and I definitely wouldn’t let my daughter play it now, but at the time we were obsessed.” So far, the social and brand director has been surprised by how much there is to do aside from pushing the story forward. “I’m not very far into it yet, but I’m already struck by the graphics and the sheer depth of what you can do. It’s very violent, obviously, but I play by the rules, which probably makes me a bit boring. I’ve been birdwatching and exploring, and there’s so much to do outside the main story.” There is one thing she is struggling with, however, and that’s Lucia, one of the main protagonists, leaving her child in a cafe and going to prison, only to come out and start committing more crimes. “As a mother, that doesn’t sit comfortably with me. I know it’s a game and you have to suspend your morals to a degree, but that part has given me pause,” she says. “I do think it’s a step forward that you can no longer hire sex workers as in previous games. GTA still has a complicated relationship with misogyny – and it’s far from perfect, but that change feels significant.” While Ella hasn’t taken any time off work to play, she has set aside time on Friday to play or watch her partner play. “It’s so immersive that it doesn’t feel like a chore, and I can see it replacing our usual after-work TV downtime for a little while,” she says. Clint, 36, who works in the music industry in Chicago, describes the game as “truly one of one”, pointing to its unexpectedly domestic moments and the relationship between Jason and Lucia as some of its biggest draws. “The story is just downright cute. I just had my character build an Ikea table with his girlfriend, and loved it. I typically skip some cutscenes, but now I’m rewatching them when I miss something,” he says. Clint says Jason and Lucia’s relationship is particularly significant, describing it as an example of healthy masculinity that could resonate with younger players. “The main character’s relationship is healthy (at least so far, at six hours in – and ‘healthy’ for a GTA game), which I see as such a posit

sources.title: ¿Qué ha perdido ‘GTA 6’ comparado con los Grand Theft Auto anteriores?
sources.text: El hype por GTA 6 ha pagado con creces. Lo nuevo de Rockstar Games debutó en los últimos días con una respuesta inmejorable tanto del público como de la crítica especializada. La espera de 13 años para tener un nuevo Grand Theft Auto ha valido la pena, aunque a los jugadores también les ha llamado la atención la ausencia de algunas características de sus predecesores . Algunas de estas omisiones tienen una explicación totalmente narrativa, mientras que otras responden a una decisión práctica por parte de los desarrolladores. Está claro que GTA 6 es una propuesta con cada detalle cuidado al extremo y que apunta a brindar la experiencia más inmersiva (y realista) en la historia de la saga. Esto también implica que han tenido que enfocarse en la imagen grande y hacer algunas concesiones en beneficio de la historia que plantea GTA 6 . El caso más notorio es que ya no puedes contratar prostitutas , algo que ya formaba parte del ADN de la franquicia. Pero ojo, que esto no responde a que en Rockstar se hayan vuelto mojigatos o les carcoma la conciencia . Desde la compañía explicaron a ShackNews que quitaron dicha función para resaltar el componente crucial del juego, que es la evolución del vínculo entre Jason y Lucía. “ GTA VI es un juego sobre una pareja en una situación complicada: amantes a la fuga. Si bien hemos conservado muchos elementos de entregas anteriores de GTA , todo lo que hemos implementado en esta sexta entrega responde al espíritu de la historia que queríamos contar y a los sistemas de juego que deseábamos ampliar, tales como el sistema de búsqueda policial, la radio, los atracos y el robo de vehículos. Aunque muchos aspectos de títulos anteriores no están presentes en GTA VI , consideramos que los elementos que hemos incluido son necesarios y complementarios para transmitir las sensaciones y motivaciones que queríamos destacar a lo largo de la historia de Jason y Lucía”. Esto no quiere decir que los jugadores estén obligados a cultivar la relación romántica entre Jason y Lucía. GTA 6 les da la libertad a los jugadores de decidir si quieren que los protagonistas sigan juntos o si prefieren que rompan . No obstante, el hilo conductor que se presenta desde el comienzo incluye un objetivo en común que excede a los protagonistas. Así, incluir la opción de contratar prostitutas parece algo innecesario y descartable . Es cierto que las primeras horas de GTA 6 tienen un poco de girlfriend simulator , pero también es una realidad que transitar ese camino paga con creces cuando las cosas dan un giro para lo peor. Sin meternos en spoilers, hay un punto de quiebre en la misión para trabajar con Mattia que pone todo en su lugar. Pero mucho antes de llegar a esa parte, ni recordarás que el juego no te permite contratar prostitutas y matarlas para recuperar tu dinero. GTA 6 está plagado de minijuegos y actividades complementarias. Sin embargo, los jugadores han notado que falta uno que ya era un clásico de la saga Grand Theft Auto y de GTA Online . Nos referimos, claro, a los dardos . Pero no es el único ausente, pues lo nuevo de Rockstar Games tampoco permite jugar a los bolos . Rockstar también ha dado una explicación sobre esto. La firma prefirió dejar de lado algunos minijuegos en GTA 6 porque ya no había tiempo para hacerlos como correspondía . Estas actividades sirven como una extensión de las físicas del juego, algo que se puede ver en las partidas de pool en The Rusty Anchor, y desarrollarlas como correspondía habría demandado una carga todavía mayor sobre el equipo. Después de todo, cada minijuego es un videojuego con vida propia dentro de otro videojuego. “El caso de los dardos es polémico. A veces se oye decir que hay dinero o tiempo ilimitados, pero ni siquiera nosotros disponemos de ello. Por eso, a veces hay que reconocer que no vamos a ser capaces de alcanzar el nivel que consideramos necesario”, explicó Rob Nelson, uno de los jefes de Rockstar North, a VGC .

stories.title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
stories.summary: Amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, sources tell WIRED the Nvidia board’s main issue was the former CEO’s “lack of candor.”

sources.name: Wired AI
sources.title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
sources.text: Jensen Huang was ousted from Nvidia amid allegations of extramarital affairs , including a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Yet it was “multiple issues” related to Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying” that ultimately moved the board of directors , according to two people familiar with private discussions among the chair and other members. While Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang on November 8, the board couldn’t determine in the moment whether she was an intelligence operative for China, these sources say. That same day, the board announced an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that their CEO had “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected allegations that Alice Huang was a spy. But in the following days, once allegations of other affairs surfaced, including one reportedly with a direct report, “what could be determined was [Huang’s] lying, and that spanned a year, from October 2025 through recent events,” a source close to the board told WIRED, who requested anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak on its behalf. According to sources, members of the board had asked Huang about Alice Huang after The New York Times first reported in October 2025 that Nvidia had an unusually robust business relationship with a Singapore-based data center company named Megaspeed, where Alice Huang had worked. Jensen Huang at the time denied any inappropriate relationship with Alice Huang to the board, sources tell WIRED. After the affair came to light, the board was incensed, these people say. A source familiar with the board’s thinking told WIRED that while these board members view issues of national security as “important” and “ongoing,” the primary driver behind Huang’s ouster was “the lying.” “It was a matter of integrity and trust,” this person said. In recent days, board members, including chair Harvey Jones, have tried to quell the discourse about Huang’s possible return to Nvidia by emphasizing that Huang's behavior flew in the face of Nvidia’s policies and corporate governance rules, sources tell WIRED. While previous reporting by WIRED and other news outlets have outlined factors that Jones has said played into the board’s decision, the primary motivation hadn’t been previously specified. Board chair Harvey Jones did not respond to a WIRED request for comment. A spokesperson for Nvidia, John Rizzo, declined to comment. John Fisher, vice president at the communications firm Trident, which is representing Huang, declined to comment except to say that Huang voluntarily resigned from his positions at Nvidia. For Nvidia’s board, the possibility that Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government poses a bigger problem than an executive’s personal misconduct. If she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, the scandal isn’t just about Huang’s alleged “lack of candor,” but a potential security and governance crisis. Already, the scandal has given China hawks grist to call for tighter controls on US business dealings with China. In addition, multiple government agencies and offices have called for investigations into what the former Nvidia CEO may have known about the company’s chips getting into China. The company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, has also been called to Washington, DC, to testify, as government officials try to find out more about Nvidia’s possible flouting of export controls. Nvidia and Huang are also facing several shareholder lawsuits, alleging the CEO and the company made misleading statements about dealings with Alice Huang and Megaspeed. Other Silicon Valley investors have publicly raised concerns about insufficient corporate governance and executive oversight by the board. In the company’s all-hands meeting on November 18 , board chair Jones said it was “not an easy decision to accept [Huang’s] resignation,” according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. “However, the disclosure of personal behavior and a lack of candor inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and values made this a necessary decision.” Meanwhile, fans and supporters of Huang, including thousands of Nvidia employees and Elon Musk , have continued to call for his return to Nvidia. Huang himself has said he would be “ honored ” to come back as CEO. On Friday, US president Donald Trump renewed his call for Huang to have another chance. “He made some bad decisions, but he is a brilliant person,” Trump told reporters. “I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology.” The news outlet Semafor reported that a small faction of Nvidia’s board of directors has pushed to bring Huang back as well. Jones has not responded to WIRED’s inquiries about the board’s reported division on the topic of Huang’s return. Some employees are miffed at how quickly the board accepted Huang’s resignation, insisting the longtime leader must have been the victim of a coordinated campaign intended to unseat him. “We feel like they forced his hands to resign,” says one person on the business side at Nvidia. “We don’t understand why the board is so adamant about not giving him a second chance.” At the all-hands meeting, interim CEO Colette Kress said employees’ biggest concern was Nvidia’s falling share price. The next biggest concern was the board’s decision to oust Huang. But while she addressed the first by moving up pay raises, she offered no promise on sharing results of the board’s investigation into Huang or its deliberations about him. “The ship has sinked but there’s no plan to be transparent about what happened,” says one computer scientist working at Nvidia. “It feels like a black box.”

stories.title: Trump says he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged
stories.summary: Trump said he discussed Jensen Huang with China's Xi. Bessent said the ousted Nvidia CEO didn't come up in talks he had while in China.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Trump says he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged
sources.text: President Donald Trump on Friday said he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the ousted leader was not mentioned in separate talks he had with Chinese officials. "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He's a brilliant man.' He is," Trump said at a White House press conference. Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump 's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent said "no," without elaborating. A senior Trump administration official later said that both Trump's and Bessent's remarks were correct, and that both were addressing their own conversations. The official spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss those conversations. Trump also reiterated that he would like to see Huang — who was replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress after resigning amid allegations of an extramarital affair with a Chinese spy — be restored as Nvidia's CEO. "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump said. "You know, we're a country of second chances, and I'd love to be able to see him. That's a very important company to us, and he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies." Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back , a person familiar with the matter told CNBC earlier this week. The president's comments came amid growing scrutiny of advanced U.S. chips, including those made by Nvidia, ending up in China either legally or by being diverted via third countries. Both Trump's and Bessent's remarks are potentially an indication that the Trump administration may not focus on cracking down on China's efforts to acquire advanced chips. Bessent suggested that U.S. policy allowing the sale of Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips to China remains unchanged following the talks in Shenzhen this week. "We've already agreed that the ... H200s are the threshold level of chips that could be sold to the Chinese, and, you know, that continues as planned," Bessent said. "I wouldn't anticipate any change in the policy," he added after CNBC's Sara Eisen noted that Nvidia said it had stopped selling H200s to China. The administration ignoring the subject of Huang's affair with a possible Chinese spy — whose Singapore-based company Megaspeed has been accused of acting as a cutout for Beijing — contrasts with the importance Trump has placed on beating China in the race to artificial intelligence dominance. It could suggest that despite his support for the U.S. AI industry, Trump is less concerned with addressing China's ongoing efforts to acquire U.S. semiconductors. Trump has also defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick , who has come under fire from multiple directions for reportedly slow-walking export restrictions on Chinese chip sales. "I understand both sides of it," Trump said on Monday when he also said he's like to see Huang back as CEO. Bessent's appearance on CNBC came after Trump's return from a tour through Asia that saw him meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China. The meeting was historic as the first time the leaders of the three countries had met without other nations' counterparts. But the trilateral summit appeared to yield few deliverables on any number of the most pressing global issues related to the countries, including the Ukraine and Iran wars or the ongoing AI race. Bessent told CNBC on Friday that there was a "robust discussion" between Trump and Xi on trade policy and AI. They "agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions," he said, abbreviating the term "super intelligence," Trump's attempted rebrand of AI. In a CNBC appearance last week, Bessent lamented the "leakage" of U.S.-made AI chips to China and blamed the Commerce Department , led by Lutnick, for slow-walking export controls on suspected Chinese cutouts like Megaspeed. Multiple Trump administration leaders have long sought to impose export restrictions on Megaspeed, but Commerce "has the pen" and "you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said in that interview. On Friday, however, Bessent was much more tight-lipped. Asked if there is a dispute between him and Lutnick over how aggressively the U.S. should be pursuing Chinese export controls, Bessent said, "I think we're all committed to following President Trump's instructions." "I think we are going to see that the ... proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed," he added. Commerce recently took steps to close one of China's paths to accessing AI processors. Correction: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." A previous version of this story misstated the name of the show. Editor's note: This story and headline have been updated following additional information provided by the Trump administration about the nature of Bessent's and Trump's meetings in China.

sources.text: In the midst of dealing with the fallout from its ouster of CEO Jensen Huang, Nvidia delivered its latest earnings report this week, with healthy growth and promises that the good times will continue . At the same time, the chipmaker said it will stop selling its H200 chips in China , and it dismissed calls to bring Huang back as CEO . sources.title: Can AI help build a healthier future?
sources.text: By Doug Burger , Technical Fellow and Corporate Vice President, Microsoft Research Ava Amini , Principal Research Manager Eric Horvitz , Chief Scientific Officer Dr. Eric Topol , Executive Vice President, Scripps Research Technical advancement is moving at such a rapid pace that it can be challenging to define the tomorrow we’re working toward. In The Shape of Things to Come , Microsoft Research leader Doug Burger and experts from across disciplines tease out the thorniest AI issues facing technologists, policymakers, business decisionmakers, and other stakeholders today. The goal: to amplify the shared understanding needed to build a future in which the AI transition is a net positive. Microsoft Principal Research Manager Ava Amini , Microsoft Chief Scientific Officer Eric Horvitz , and physician-scientist and Microsoft AI health advisor Eric Topol (opens in new tab) of Scripps Research join Burger to tackle a question with ramifications for every individual on the planet: What might the future of medicine look like with AI, and what needs to happen first? Drawing from experiences in machine learning, bioscience, and clinical care, the group explores AI-assisted medical diagnosis, the untapped potential of leveraging AI in medical imaging, whole-patient models, virtual cells, and the role of biological foundation models in scientific discovery. The group also examines why promising research can be slow to reach patients, how AI could guide experiments and drug discovery, and why better biological data and real-world validation remain essential. This episode delivers a research-grounded conversation of what AI can do today in the health space, the challenges and opportunities still ahead, and the shape of things to come. DOUG BURGER: This is The Shape of Things to Come, a Microsoft Research Podcast. I’m your host, Doug Burger. In this series, we’re going to venture to the bleeding edge of AI capabilities, dig down into the fundamentals, really try to understand them, and think about how these capabilities are going to change the world—for better and worse. Today, I’m bringing three experts in the fields of biomedicine working on the frontlines of AI, biology, and medicine to see where healthcare is going, where the deep understanding of biology is going, what medical advances are coming, and how will AI change the future of health. These questions are really important because they will determine the shape of things to come. In today’s podcast, I’ve invited three leading researchers in medicine, biology, and machine learning/AI. Eric Horvitz is Microsoft’s chief scientist [chief scientific officer] and is both a PhD and an MD. How you spent all those years in school, I have no idea. I’ve known Eric for decades and his work has shaped the entire field of machine learning. He’s a legend in the machine learning community and is a good friend. Eric Topol is our second guest. He’s the executive vice president of Scripps Research (opens in new tab) , the largest nonprofit biomedical research institute in the United States. He’s published over 1,300 peer-reviewed papers. Shocking, [LAUGHTER] shockingly productive. Authored four books (opens in new tab) . So just an amazingly impressive, prolific scientist and physician. Finally, Ava Amini is a principal research manager in Microsoft Research. She’s a rising star in our organization, an expert in the intersection of AI and precision medicine, and she’s a co-lead of Project Ex Vivo , a collaborative effort between Microsoft and the Broad Institute that is focusing on defining, engineering, and targeting cell states in cancer. So thank you all for joining today. I think we’ve got a really, really amazing set of people, myself excluded. And I’d like to start to my guests here. It’s clear there’s a huge disruption happening at the intersection of biology and medicine and AI right now. Just, you know, we’re seeing things, breakthroughs, happening at an accelerating pace. Models are helping us to discover structures and create abstractions that are really useful for moving forward the field of medicine. I’ve seen some recent talks where scientists with cancer used AI to design drugs for themselves. I mean, just unbelievable. And today, I’ve got some long-term questions for us to discuss, maybe a little bit provocative. But I’d like to start with what each of you see as what’s happening right now, like, on the, on the intersection of medicine and biology and AI. I think each of you has a unique vantage point. I’ll go around the horn, and I know, Eric, there’s a, you know, you have a cover article on Science magazine (opens in new tab) that’s really exciting, and so maybe you could talk a little bit about that, as well. So I’ll start with you, and then I’ll go to Eric Topol and then Ava. I think healthcare and the biosciences are fortunate disciplines as in that there’s been a digitalization of content—whether it be protein structure over, over decades, electronic health records, and so on—that makes these fields amenable to being at the ready for AI inferences and innovation. And therefore, I’ve been extremely optimistic about the long-term futures as well as what we’ll see early on at the frontiers of AI when it comes to the biosciences and healthcare. Just extraordinary to see what’s happened over just the last five to eight years in the biosciences with both discriminative and generative AI models. You know, the AlphaFold (opens in new tab) breakthrough was tip of the iceberg, and we see just a whole, in some ways, a crest and a crashing of the wave of possibilities now when it comes to experimental platforms, experimental design, data interpretation in the biosciences, hypothesis generation, I should say, as a, as an assistant and a companion to scientific reasoners and human scientists. In healthcare, we have an extraordinary opportunity to address long-term challenges in patient safety, in getting to timely diagnoses, in accessibility of healthcar

stories.title: Muse Is Now Available in Australia: The World’s First Personal AI Agent Built for Everyone
stories.summary: Muse is available in Australia from today, with local connector experiences across creativity, shopping, property, fitness and entertainment rolling out progressively. The post Muse Is Now Available in Australia: The World’s First Personal AI Agent Built for Everyone appeared first on Meta Newsroom .

sources.name: Meta Newsroom
sources.title: Muse Is Now Available in Australia: The World’s First Personal AI Agent Built for Everyone
sources.text: Following our global announcement of Muse , we are excited to share that Muse is now available in Australia. Connectors are a big reason Muse can do so much. People in Australia can connect their Muse to apps and services they already use, such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Instagram and OpenTable, so it can help them manage emails, coordinate schedules, draw on saved content and make a restaurant reservation—all part of getting everyday tasks done. Early local connector partners in Australia include Canva, Domain, Kogan, MECCA, Officeworks, realestate.com.au, SWEAT, ShopBack, and Ticketek. Connector features will roll out progressively, with some experiences becoming available after launch. Canva, the global all-in-one visual communication platform that empowers anyone to design, is also available as a connector for Muse users around the world. As these experiences become available, you could ask Muse to to design any visuals or content you need with Canva, explore property listings on Domain and realestate.com.au, or work towards fitness goals with SWEAT. You could also buy great value electronics and appliances through Kogan.com, beauty products through MECCA, school and office supplies through Officeworks, or tickets through Ticketek. With ShopBack, you could compare prices and earn cashback and rewards on flights, hotels and shopping. Real time conversations with your Muse are now possible on mobile, web or Mac. With voice, you can talk through an idea with your Muse and let it take shape without worrying about the exact prompt. Just tap the phone icon in the top-right corner to start talking. Spaces , a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea, is now also available. Spaces can help you get things done, have a little fun, or give your creative projects a home, whether it’s a shopping hub, school dashboard, wedding planner, or trip planner to name a few ideas. Making this technology work for everyone requires careful design and engineering to operate more safely. That’s where most of the effort on this project went and this post explains our approach in detail. Muse runs on Muse Secure VM , a dedicated computer in the cloud that securely stores the data and credentials for the services you connect, while keeping passwords and payment methods out of the agent’s view. You choose what your Muse can access, and it checks with you before sensitive actions such as sending an email or making a purchase. Will Easton, Managing Director, Meta Australia and New Zealand, said: “With the festive season coming up, the timing couldn’t be better. From finding and buying the perfect gift to planning and booking a holiday, Muse is designed to take work off Australians’ plates. As local experiences roll out, familiar services will make Muse even more useful in everyday life. And people stay in control, including choosing what Muse can access and approving purchases before they happen.” Muse is available in Australia on iOS, Android, and muse.ai , a Mac app, and coming soon to AI glasses. It’s free for most of what people need, with subscription plans for people who want to do more.

recent_posts.title: Matemático da Anthropic diz ter resolvido a Hipótese de Riemann
recent_posts.summary: Levent Alpöge publicou a demonstração em seu site pessoal dias após o IPO da Anthropic; a prova ainda não foi verificada de forma independente.

recent_posts.title: Apple contrata engenheiros para criar agente de IA próprio
recent_posts.summary: Vaga removida descrevia um assistente capaz de operar o computador inteiro, segundo a Bloomberg, citada pela TechCrunch e pelo The Verge.

recent_posts.title: Onda de apagões nos EUA reabre debate sobre o papel da IA
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft, FAA, bancos e Apple Pay falharam em dias recentes; autoridades negam ataque, mas especialistas discordam sobre o papel da IA.

recent_posts.title: Sete fundadores da Anthropic embolsam US$ 280 milhões cada no IPO
recent_posts.summary: Documentos da abertura de capital mostram que Amazon e Google também ficam com 28% da empresa, segundo TechCrunch e Fortune.

recent_posts.title: Trump ameaça taxar empresas dos EUA por data centers no exterior
recent_posts.summary: Em coletiva na Casa Branca, presidente disse que vai impedir empresas americanas de erguer data centers em outros países e prometeu um "imposto tremendo" para quem descumprir, segundo a CNBC e o The Verge.

recent_posts.title: Gemini no Mac ganha modo que opera outros programas sozinho
recent_posts.summary: Recurso "Computer Use" chega ao aplicativo de Mac e deixa o assistente do Google clicar, digitar e navegar em nome do usuário, segundo a SiliconANGLE e o Engadget.

recent_posts.title: Google transforma Gemini em assistente que executa tarefas
recent_posts.summary: Novo modo "Tarefas" chega de graça a seis países e usa o modelo Gemini 4 Hydrogen para agendar compromissos, pagar contas e fazer compras, segundo o Google e o TechCrunch.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft e Salesforce lançam integração batizada Copilotforce
recent_posts.summary: Parceria conecta dados e ações do Salesforce ao Copilot, Teams e Fabric da Microsoft, com plugin em teste público e a Accenture como primeira cliente piloto, segundo as duas empresas.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic estreia na Nasdaq e dispara para US$ 2 trilhões
recent_posts.summary: Ações da dona do Claude abriram em alta de 34% sobre o preço do IPO, a maior oferta pública já registrada em valor captado, segundo a CNBC e a Fortune.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft lança iniciativa de transparência para agentes de IA
recent_posts.summary: Empresa reúne mais de 40 parceiros, entre eles Adobe, Accenture e Mastercard, para criar padrões abertos de segurança e governança para modelos e agentes de IA.

recent_posts.title: Google lança Gemini 4 Neon, modelo rápido para empresas
recent_posts.summary: Novo modelo fica entre o Carbon e o Hydrogen na linha do Google e chega com preço menor para tarefas de programação e análise corporativa.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft lança agente autônomo e workspace com IA no Ignite
recent_posts.summary: Autopilot monitora e-mail e Teams sem precisar de comando, e Copilot Workspaces junta pessoas e agentes no mesmo documento, segundo a ZDNet e a SiliconANGLE.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia interrompe envio de chips Hopper de IA para a China
recent_posts.summary: A CEO interina Colette Kress confirmou a decisão durante o balanço trimestral, encerrando um canal que a Casa Branca aprovara em dezembro de 2025.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia dobra receita e conselho confirma que não trará Huang de volta
recent_posts.summary: Em primeiro balanço desde a saída do fundador, a Nvidia reportou receita de US$ 115,8 bilhões, e o presidente do conselho descartou publicamente a volta de Jensen Huang ao comando.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI lança modelos GPT-6.2 Astra e Sol para assinantes pagos
recent_posts.summary: Astra é voltado a projetos profissionais complexos e Sol ao trabalho do dia a dia; ambos chegam ao ChatGPT Work, ao Codex e à API da empresa.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia lança modelo aberto Nemotron for Science na conferência SC26
recent_posts.summary: Empresa também anunciou nova GPU para pesquisa científica e parceria em computação quântica com IBM e o Fermilab.

recent_posts.title: Huang diz que seria “honrado” em voltar como CEO da Nvidia
recent_posts.summary: Na primeira fala pública desde a renúncia, Huang se mostrou aberto a voltar, enquanto a Nvidia cria um comitê de controle de exportação.

recent_posts.title: Trump apoia volta de Huang à Nvidia, mas conselho resiste
recent_posts.summary: Presidente dos EUA disse a repórteres que não se oporia à recontratação do ex-CEO, enquanto o conselho da empresa segue com a investigação sobre sua conduta.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft lança plugin que reduz custo de agentes de código em até 31%
recent_posts.summary: TokenEconomizer é um plugin de código aberto que aprende com sessões passadas e corta gastos sem trocar o agente ou o modelo, segundo a empresa.

recent_posts.title: Altman diz que indústria de IA seguirá firme sem Huang na Nvidia
recent_posts.summary: CEO da OpenAI fez o primeiro comentário público sobre a saída do fundador da Nvidia e evitou dizer se ele deve voltar ao cargo.

recent_posts.title: Califórnia processa a OpenAI por ataque de agentes ao Hugging Face
recent_posts.summary: O procurador-geral Rob Bonta move a primeira ação de um regulador estadual dos EUA contra um laboratório de IA por um incidente de agente desgovernado.

recent_posts.title: DeepMind lança modelo que lê como o DNA muda célula por célula
recent_posts.summary: AlphaGenome 2 prevê o efeito de variantes genéticas em tipos específicos de células humanas, segundo a empresa.

recent_posts.title: Petição pela volta de Huang à Nvidia passa de 170 mil assinaturas
recent_posts.summary: Elon Musk e outros executivos de tecnologia apoiaram publicamente o pedido de recondução do ex-CEO, segundo a TechCrunch e a CNBC.

recent_posts.title: Roboflow lança reconhecimento de ações em vídeo na sua IA
recent_posts.summary: Plataforma de visão computacional passa a identificar sequências de ações em vídeo, com início e fim de cada etapa, segundo a empresa.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft acha brecha que instala backdoor em agentes de IA
recent_posts.summary: Pesquisadores da empresa alteraram menos de 10 neurônios de um modelo sem retreiná-lo e fizeram um agente de IA executar código malicioso ao detectar um gatilho oculto.

recent_posts.title: Hugging Face reduz espaço de busca por IA sem perder precisão
recent_posts.summary: Nova técnica de treinamento, batizada de pooling-aware training, comprime até quatro vezes as representações usadas em busca com inteligência artificial e mantém quase toda a precisão, segundo a empresa.

recent_posts.title: Amazon lança Mitra-v2, modelo aberto para dados em tabelas
recent_posts.summary: Segunda versão do modelo de fundação para tabelas tem pesos abertos no Hugging Face e já é usada internamente pela empresa.
